name: Not Invented Here
description: Teams devalue external ideas, tools, or solutions simply because they came from outside the group. 'Ours' feels safer, smarter, or more legitimate than something imported, even when the outside option is better.
design_relevance_note: Directly relevant to build-vs-buy decisions, reluctance to adopt external design systems or research findings, and organizational habits of reinventing components rather than reusing proven outside solutions.
myth_risk_note: The core finding (declining external-knowledge uptake) replicates, but the popular 'universal NIH bias' shorthand is broader than the evidence supports — the effect depends on the knowledge source (stronger toward competitors than suppliers) and firm success/identity, not a blanket organizational tendency.
prevalence_note: A standard phrase in engineering, platform, and product-organization debates about build-vs-buy and internal reimplementation, even though it is less consumer-facing than most UX heuristics.

findings.description: A mixed-methods study (32 interviews/3 focus groups plus a quantitative survey of 565 global R&D projects) confirmed the Not-Invented-Here Syndrome is prevalent and reduces project success by impeding external-knowledge absorption. Perspective-taking -- an indirect debiasing technique that attenuates the behavioral impact of the negative attitude without directly confronting it -- was empirically shown to be an effective countermeasure, a genuinely actionable, design/practice-relevant intervention this corpus didn't previously have for this entry.
findings.effect_size: Quantitative survey of 565 global R&D projects
findings.source_title: Containing the Not-Invented-Here Syndrome in external knowledge absorption and open innovation: The role of indirect countermeasures

findings.description: In 50 R&D project groups, performance eventually declined as tenure increased and communication with critical external sources fell off. The paper treats this reduced openness to outside knowledge as a real organizational problem under the Not Invented Here label.
findings.source_title: Investigating the Not Invented Here (NIH) syndrome: A look at the performance, tenure, and communication patterns of 50 R & D Project Groups

findings.description: The Not-Invented-Here Syndrome is not a blanket organizational tendency: internal resistance to external knowledge is significantly more likely when that knowledge comes from competitors than from suppliers, customers, or universities, and is stronger in successful firms -- consistent with social-identity-theory predictions that firm success increases employee identification and in-group favoritism, strengthening rejection of externally-sourced (competitor) knowledge specifically.
findings.source_title: In search for the not-invented-here syndrome: the role of knowledge sources and firm success

applications.title: SC Johnson Germany nearly missed a product because it came from the wrong subsidiary
applications.description: Rolf-Christian Wentz, writing about his own tenure as managing director of SC Johnson's German subsidiary, describes how an innovative air-freshener product developed and successfully launched by the company's Asian subsidiary was largely ignored by the U.S. headquarters, apparently due in part to a bias favoring innovations that originated domestically. The German subsidiary happened to learn of the Asian product by chance, adapted it minimally, and launched it as Brise One Touch -- which went on to take a 50% leadership share of its local product category and later succeeded in other markets. Wentz also cites a survey of 565 innovation projects worldwide finding that only 16% were entirely unaffected by NIH bias, which correlated with reduced project success.
applications.industry_context: consumer packaged goods (household air fresheners), multinational subsidiary structure
applications.ethical_note: Illustrates an organizational bias against internally-sourced-but-foreign ideas costing a real, quantifiable market opportunity until chance intervened -- no manipulation of end users is involved.
